classification.difficultyReason: Translate an angle of elevation and horizontal distance into a tangent calculation for a vertical height.

content.prompt: The angle of elevation of the top of a building from a point $30\text{ m}$ from its base is $55^{\circ}$. Calculate the height of the building to 1 d.p.

spec.description: Observer at the left, horizontal ground to the building at the right, dashed ascending sightline to the building top, and a right-angle marker at the base. Decorative windows and doorway are omitted; the building remains an unshaded editable outline.
spec.mathematics: The building height is perpendicular to the horizontal ground. The sightline joins the observer to the building top. No lengths, angles or unknown labels are printed in the source diagram.
spec.answerVisibility: Given geometry only; no teacher answer or calculated height.

answer.worked:
Let $h$ be the height of the building in metres.
$$\begin{align*}\tan 55^{\circ} &= \frac{h}{30} \\ 30\tan 55^{\circ} &= h \\ h &\approx 42.8\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
